items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: to play music to that level like Elvin Jones or Jack DeJohnette or Miles Davis or Wayne Shorter or Duke Ellington, you have to be unbelievably brilliant

ctx.x: It’s never easy and I don’t ever think about the money part of it. And I probably should if I was more wise that way I would maybe get a lot more money but all of the projects are just like this is what I want to do and somehow I’m going to make it happen somehow, like the “Jazz Griots” is just like this project with Jordan Walker-Pearlman and he’s a film director in L.A. And only because I was on a flight going from New York to L.A. I was sitting next to a gentleman who is a producer and he’s a lawyer but he’s…

they’re just like being nice. Turns out he was being nice and he got back to New York, sure enough I met with this director Jordan Walker-Pearlman. He goes, “I hear you have ideas for movies.” And I actually took out a list of like ten ideas. And he looks at these ideas and he goes, “I think we should do that one first, what do you think?” I said, “Yeah.” He goes, “Okay let’s start.” And believe it or not we filmed already two and then right before the pandemic so we’re trying to now start again. But it’s my idea…

items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Tim Ries came in and played saxophones on the recording.

ctx.x: Well, this was a project through the encouragement and suggestion of my wife Lydia, through the associations that we have with Chuck Mitchell, who is a great

friend and supporter of my music and things that I did. Chuck’s been involved in television, and with projects, which involve Herbie Hancock. We spoke to Chuck as the economy and our country and around the world is changing, and as things are getting a little tighter… We considered maybe not doing this, having a record label. Stuff like that. Lydia said, “Let’s call Chuck and see if he has some suggestions,” and so we called. Chuck came up and had some ideas. I have to interject, getting the NEA award was…
Which is one of the reasons that we got the phone call that you had a day.
